name: ALTA EQUIPMENT GROUP INC CLASS A

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The strongest counter is that the announcement partially VINDICATES the bull case the 2026-09-03 devil's advocate made and I dismissed - that a correctly-levered equity stub in a turning cycle is where the biggest returns are. Viking Global, a serious institution with full access to the data room, has agreed to put $338.4 million into this company at $6.33 a share on an as-converted basis, a 1.8% premium to the $6.22 price, when the entire public market capitalisation is $203.2M. That is an outside professional investor underwriting roughly 1.7x the whole public equity at above the market price, having seen the real obligation stack I have spent two passes reconstructing. It also delivers exactly what my prior watch list demanded - 'the first real evidence of deleveraging' - not through operations but through a recapitalisation, plus a credible path to the 2.0-3.0x leverage target and $170M of NOLs. On that reading my refusal is a failure to recognise that someone with better information has just priced the equity, and priced it above the market.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: The proxy for the stockholder vote, which will carry the full Series B terms - conversion mechanics, any dividend or liquidation preference ahead of common, anti-dilution, and whether the economic pari passu claim survives contact with the actual certificate of designations. And the pro-forma capitalisation and leverage table in that proxy, which settles both the share count and the obligation stack in one filed document.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Two things are visible and they are why the counter does not get me to a number rather than to a different verdict. First, the guidance cut: the prior pass nominated 'Q3/Q4 Adjusted EBITDA against the $167.5-177.5M full-year guide' as its settling test, and the answer came in BELOW the prior range at both ends, at $165.0-170.0M. The test ran and failed. Second, the deleveraging test also effectively failed: the line of credit fell from $213.6M at 2025-12-31 to $192.9M and total debt and finance leases from $735.0M to $710.7M, but used-and-rental floor plan rose from $72.3M to $87.8M, so total obligations fell roughly $12M on a ~$1,036M stack over nine months - about 1%. What the counter has that I cannot refute is Viking's own price, and the honest response to a sophisticated third party paying $6.33 is not to argue the equity is worthless; it is to say the per-share arithmetic is about to change by a factor of three and no number should be published until it has.
devils_advocate.unresolved: I could not read the Series B certificate of designations - the press release says 'economic rights that are pari passu with Alta common stock' and the definitive documents are not yet filed, so I do not know whether there is a dividend, a liquidation preference, or anti-dilution that sits ahead of common in practice. I also could not get the new-equipment floor plan interest cost separately, nor split maintenance from growth rental-fleet capex (the same gap as the prior pass); on this name the AROC rescue is unavailable anyway because the extractor captures only 7% of the fleet spend. And JGP's standalone EBITDA is given only inside the combined $226M figure, so I cannot test the $399M enterprise value against JGP's own earnings.

what_changed: A transformative, pending transaction announced 2026-11-23 under 8-K items 1.01, 3.02, 5.02, 7.01, 8.01 and 9.01, with a filed press release and investor presentation - four days before the price date, and the cause of the +22.7% five-day move on 3.0x volume that won the opportunistic slot. Alta has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Jackson Group Peterbilt, a 34-location commercial-truck dealership platform in the western US, at an enterprise value of about $399M, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. It is financed by a $338.4 million strategic investment from entities managed by Viking Global Investors into new Series B Convertible Preferred Stock, priced at the 60-day VWAP of $6.33 per share on an as-converted basis, non-voting, with economic rights pari passu with common, plus $30 million of deal consideration in common stock at $6.33 to the seller. Viking gets two board seats, a non-voting observer and consent rights over certain significant corporate actions. Combined trailing-twelve-month figures to 2026-09-30 are approximately $2.7 billion of revenue and $226 million of adjusted EBITDA; the combination is said to lift aftermarket contribution to gross profit to 59% and absorption from 77% to 89%, with a new leverage target of 2.0-3.0x and approximately $170M of federal NOLs potentially usable. Closing requires Alta STOCKHOLDER approval of the share issuance. Separately, Q3 2026 (2026-11-09) cut full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $165.0-170.0M from the $167.5-177.5M the prior pass was told to test, and reported a Q3 loss against estimates.
consensus_case: Alta is a levered equipment-dealer stub whose equity is a thin residual on a large obligation stack, and four days before the price date it agreed to a transaction that roughly triples the as-converted share count. At 2026-09-30 total debt and finance leases were $710.7M, plus $237.9M of new-equipment and $87.8M of used-and-rental floor plan - about $1,036M of obligations - against a $203.2M market capitalisation and NEGATIVE book equity of $36.2M at 2026-06-30. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was CUT on 2026-11-09 to $165.0-170.0M on material-handling delivery delays. So the market is paying roughly 1.2x the equity residual of a 4.2x-levered dealer in a cycle that has not yet turned into cash: nine months of 'recovery' reduced the line of credit from $213.6M to $192.9M while used-and-rental floor plan ROSE from $72.3M to $87.8M, a net reduction of about 1% of the stack. That is the market's case and it is a reasonable one.
base_case_rationale: No valuation is recordable, and this is a verdict CHANGE from the 2026-09-03 pass, which recorded no_edge with a number described as an upper bound. The reason is the Viking transaction: $338.4M of Series B convertible preferred at $6.33 as-converted plus $30M of common to the seller is roughly 58.2 million new as-converted shares against 32,666,872 outstanding, so the as-converted count goes to about 90.9 million - the existing equity is diluted to roughly 36% of the company - and the preferred's economic rights are pari passu with common. Any per-share figure computed on 32.7M shares is therefore meaningless, and the schema has no field to reach it. That sits on top of three defects this file has already documented on this ticker and verified again today as verbatim unchanged. total_debt is $497.2M (the $500M second-lien notes net of issuance costs and discount) against $710.7M of debt and finance leases in the Q3 10-Q plus $325.7M of floor plan - so between $213M and $539M of obligations are invisible, and interest_expense of $88.4M over the recorded $497.2M is an implied 17.8%, impossible against stated coupons of 9.00%. capex_series of [$9.2M, $15.4M, $12.4M] against dep_amort_series of [$133.6M, $144.5M, $132.6M] is a D&A-to-capex ratio of 14.5x, far above the 5x threshold, on a company with a rental fleet - the CTOS and WLFC omission. And of the $105.2M FCFF base, about $66.3M - 63% - is the after-tax interest add-back on debt the model cannot see, which is the SABR condition.
key_risks: A pending $338.4M Series B convertible preferred issuance at $6.33 plus $30M of common consideration takes the as-converted count from 32.7M to about 90.9M - existing holders diluted to roughly 36%
Total obligations of about $1,036M ($710.7M of debt and finance leases plus $325.7M of floor plan) against a $203.2M market capitalisation; book equity was NEGATIVE $36.2M at 2026-06-30
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was CUT to $165.0-170.0M, below the prior range at both ends, on material-handling delivery delays
The transaction requires a stockholder vote and regulatory approvals and may not close; the +22.7% five-day move already prices approval
Beta 2.5 at R-squared 0.414 gives a 17.6% WACC, so the discount rate dominates any valuation and the schema cannot override it
Viking receives two board seats and consent rights over certain significant corporate actions, so control economics change as well as the share count
watch_for: The proxy statement for the share-issuance vote - the Series B certificate of designations and the pro-forma capitalisation and leverage table settle both the count and the stack
Whether the stockholder vote passes and the transaction closes in Q1 2027 as guided
JGP's standalone adjusted EBITDA, disclosed separately rather than inside the combined $226M
Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA against the cut $165.0-170.0M guide
Total floor plan plus line of credit at year end - whether the recapitalisation is used to retire obligations or to fund the purchase
